message: ACE inhibitors cause fetal toxicity (renal failure, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia), particularly in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
recommendation: Stop and switch to a pregnancy-safe antihypertensive (e.g. labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa).
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: ARBs cause fetal toxicity (renal failure, oligohydramnios, skull hypoplasia), particularly in the 2nd and 3rd trimesters.
recommendation: Stop and switch to a pregnancy-safe antihypertensive (e.g. labetalol, nifedipine, methyldopa).
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Warfarin crosses the placenta: embryopathy in the 1st trimester and fetal bleeding later.
recommendation: Switch to low-molecular-weight heparin under specialist advice.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Misoprostol is an abortifacient and teratogen.
recommendation: Do not use in pregnancy unless for an obstetric indication under specialist care.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Isotretinoin is a potent teratogen.
recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy; require reliable contraception.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Leflunomide is teratogenic.
recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Mycophenolate causes miscarriage and congenital malformations.
recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy unless no alternative, under specialist care.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Thalidomide causes severe birth defects.
recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Ribavirin is teratogenic.
recommendation: Contraindicated in pregnancy.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Statins are generally avoided in pregnancy.
recommendation: Stop in pregnancy unless there is a compelling indication; specialist advice.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Tetracyclines can affect fetal teeth and bone development, mainly after the first trimester.
recommendation: Use a pregnancy-appropriate antibiotic.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Fluoroquinolones are generally avoided in pregnancy.
recommendation: Use an alternative antibiotic if possible.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: NSAIDs are best avoided in pregnancy, especially from 20 weeks (oligohydramnios, ductus arteriosus constriction).
recommendation: Use paracetamol for analgesia.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Co-trimoxazole near term can cause neonatal kernicterus, and trimethoprim is a folate antagonist in the first trimester.
recommendation: Use an alternative where possible.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Lithium is associated with cardiac malformations in the first trimester.
recommendation: Specialist review; do not stop abruptly.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Methotrexate is excreted in breast milk and can cause infant toxicity.
recommendation: Do not breastfeed during treatment.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Amiodarone and its iodine content pass into breast milk (infant thyroid effects).
recommendation: Avoid breastfeeding or use an alternative.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Codeine can cause life-threatening infant opioid toxicity in ultra-rapid metabolisers.
recommendation: Avoid in breastfeeding; use another analgesic.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Tramadol passes into breast milk and may cause infant sedation or breathing difficulty.
recommendation: Prefer an alternative analgesic; monitor the infant if essential.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Lithium reaches high levels in breast milk.
recommendation: Specialist review; monitor the infant and drug levels.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Cyclophosphamide is excreted in breast milk and is cytotoxic.
recommendation: Do not breastfeed during treatment.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review

message: Leflunomide is not recommended during breastfeeding.
recommendation: Do not breastfeed during treatment.
source: Standard prescribing references (product labels, national formularies); pending clinical review
